guide.summary: Use Linear OAuth 2.0 with the user actor and the documented read scope, then test issue-title reads against the GraphQL API for one test account. Pagination uses documented cursor arguments: an initial page, then continuation with the returned endCursor until hasNextPage is false. The read scope covers the connected user's account, not only issues, so disclose that boundary. Customer-facing distribution rules for user-actor OAuth are not established by the sources and must be verified before rollout. No mutation calls are needed.

steps.title: Test reading issue titles
steps.detail: Send an authorized GraphQL read for issue titles to the Linear endpoint using the OAuth Bearer token. Expected response: a data.issues.nodes array of objects with id and title. Boundary check: confirm the response contains no errors and that the outgoing request log shows only this query.
steps.doneWhen: The response lists issue titles for the test workspace.

evidence.quote: --data '{ "query": "{ issues { nodes { id title } } }" }' \
with the header `Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>`

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"{ issues { nodes { id title } } }"}'

steps.title: Test the first paginated issue-title page
steps.detail: Request the first page with first: 10 and read pageInfo. Expected response: id and title nodes plus pageInfo.hasNextPage and pageInfo.endCursor. Boundary check: confirm the request is a read query only and no mutation appears in the request log.
steps.doneWhen: The first page returns nodes and pageInfo, and endCursor is recorded when hasNextPage is true.

evidence.quote: } ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
hasNextPage endCursor } }

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"{ issues(first: 10) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}'

steps.title: Test the continuation page and repeat until complete
steps.detail: Send the same query with after set to the endCursor from the previous response. Repeat this step, replacing the cursor each time, while pageInfo.hasNextPage is true. Stop when hasNextPage is false. Expected response: the next set of id and title nodes starting after the prior cursor. Boundary check: confirm every request is a read query and no mutation appears in the request log.
steps.doneWhen: A second page returns nodes after the first endCursor, and the loop ends when hasNextPage is false.

evidence.quote: } ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
and you'll paginate through all the values in the collection.

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"{ issues(first: 10, after: \"<CURSOR>\") { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}'
